lecture.New_Day10Part1audio01.mp3: Welcome to Day 10! Today marks a monumental milestone in your SQL journey: mastering Table Joins. In relational database architecture, data is normalized across multiple tables to avoid duplication. Joins allow you to stitch related tables back together into comprehensive analytical datasets.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio02.mp3: Joins work through relationships between Primary Keys and Foreign Keys. A primary key uniquely identifies each row in a parent table, while a foreign key in a child table references that primary key to establish relational integrity.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio03.mp3: The foundational join type is the INNER JOIN. An INNER JOIN evaluates a join condition and returns only rows that have matching records in both tables. Any unmatched row from either table is completely excluded.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio04.mp3: Always use concise table aliases! Writing orders AS o and customers AS c keeps queries readable and avoids repetitive typing when prefixing columns.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio05.mp3: In Query 1, we join the orders table with the customers table using customer ID. Notice how each order is seamlessly enriched with the purchasing customer's name and region.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio06.mp3: Real-world queries frequently join three or more tables. SQL processes multi-table joins sequentially, matching the first two tables and then joining subsequent tables to the intermediate result.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio07.mp3: In Query 2, we connect order items to orders, and then connect to products. This allows us to inspect the specific product names, item quantities, and order dates for every transaction.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio08.mp3: Combining joins with GROUP BY and aggregate functions unlocks immense business intelligence. You can group by customer or category name to calculate revenue, average order value, and order frequencies.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio09.mp3: Now, let's explore the LEFT OUTER JOIN, commonly called LEFT JOIN. Unlike INNER JOIN, a LEFT JOIN preserves every single row from the left table, even if there is no corresponding match in the right table.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio10.mp3: When a left row has no match, the database fills all columns from the right table with NULL values. This prevents silent data loss when auditing customer bases or product catalogs.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio11.mp3: In Query 3, we perform a LEFT JOIN from customers to orders. Customers who haven't placed an order still appear with NULL for order ID, giving us complete visibility across our customer base.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio12.mp3: The Anti-Join pattern is a high-value data analytics technique. By combining a LEFT JOIN with a WHERE right table key IS NULL clause, you can isolate churned customers, unsold products, or empty departments in milliseconds.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio13.mp3: In Query 4, we use the Anti-Join pattern to pinpoint inactive customers who registered but have never placed an order.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio14.mp3: Beware the classic ON versus WHERE clause trap! If you filter a right table column in the WHERE clause, any NULL-padded row fails the check, unintentionally turning your LEFT JOIN back into an INNER JOIN! Always place right-table filters in the ON clause to preserve left rows.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio15.mp3: Database support: SQLite and MySQL natively support INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, and CROSS JOIN. PostgreSQL and modern enterprise warehouses also support RIGHT JOIN and FULL OUTER JOIN.
lecture.New_Day10Part1audio16.mp3: You now possess the foundational join mechanics essential for professional data analysis. Let's enter the practice arena and query multi-table relationships!

questions.New_Day10Question01.mp3: Enrich orders with customer names! Perform an INNER JOIN between orders and customers on customer ID. Return order ID, customer first name, last name, order date, and total amount.
questions.New_Day10Question01sol.mp3: Let's join orders and customers. SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, o.order_date, o.total_amount... FROM orders o INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id.
questions.New_Day10Question02.mp3: Map products to categories! Join the products table with categories on category ID equals categories ID. Return product ID, product name, category name, and unit price.
questions.New_Day10Question02sol.mp3: Let's map product categories. SELECT p.product_id, p.name AS product_name, c.name AS category_name, p.unit_price... FROM products p INNER JOIN categories c ON p.category_id = c.id.
questions.New_Day10Question03.mp3: Department staffing overview! Join employees with departments on department ID. Return employee ID, first name, last name, job title, and department name.
questions.New_Day10Question03sol.mp3: Let's link employees to departments. SELECT e.employee_id, e.first_name, e.last_name, e.job_title, d.department_name... FROM employees e INNER JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.department_id.
questions.New_Day10Question04.mp3: Three-table join on line items! Join order items with orders and products. Return order ID, order date, product name, quantity, and item unit price.
questions.New_Day10Question04sol.mp3: Let's join three tables. SELECT oi.order_id, o.order_date, p.name AS product_name, oi.qty, oi.unit_price... FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id.
questions.New_Day10Question05.mp3: Total customer spending! Join customers with orders to compute total revenue per customer. Return customer ID, first name, last name, and total spending, sorted by spending descending.
questions.New_Day10Question05sol.mp3: Let's aggregate customer revenue. SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name, SUM of o.total_amount AS total_spent... FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id... GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.last_name... ORDER BY total_spent DESC.
questions.New_Day10Question06.mp3: Category sales volume! Join categories with products, grouping by category name to return category name, product count, and average unit price rounded to 2 decimals.
questions.New_Day10Question06sol.mp3: Let's summarize product categories. SELECT c.name AS category_name, COUNT of p.product_id AS product_count, ROUND of AVG of p.unit_price, 2 AS avg_price... FROM categories c INNER JOIN products p ON c.id = p.category_id... GROUP BY c.name... ORDER BY product_count DESC.
questions.New_Day10Question07.mp3: Auditing all customers with LEFT JOIN! Perform a LEFT JOIN from customers to orders. Return customer ID, first name, and count of orders placed, including customers with zero orders.
questions.New_Day10Question07sol.mp3: Let's count orders per customer including zero. SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, COUNT of o.order_id AS order_count... FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id... GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.first_name... ORDER BY order_count DESC.
questions.New_Day10Question08.mp3: Identify inactive customers using an Anti-Join! Perform a LEFT JOIN from customers to orders and filter for customers who have never placed an order, returning customer ID, first name, and email.
questions.New_Day10Question08sol.mp3: Let's find customers without orders. SELECT c.customer_id, c.first_name, c.email... FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id... WHERE o.order_id IS NULL.
questions.New_Day10Question09.mp3: Audit empty product categories! Perform a LEFT JOIN from categories to products. Return category ID, category name, and count of associated products, ordered from least to most.
questions.New_Day10Question09sol.mp3: Let's inspect categories with LEFT JOIN. SELECT c.id AS category_id, c.name AS category_name, COUNT of p.product_id AS product_count... FROM categories c LEFT JOIN products p ON c.id = p.category_id... GROUP BY c.id, c.name... ORDER BY product_count ASC.
questions.New_Day10Question10.mp3: Order line items breakdown! Join order items with products on product ID. Return order ID, product name, quantity, unit price, and extended line total as qty multiplied by unit price.
questions.New_Day10Question10sol.mp3: Let's calculate line totals. SELECT oi.order_id, p.name AS product_name, oi.qty, oi.unit_price, oi.qty * oi.unit_price AS line_total... FROM order_items oi INNER JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id.
questions.New_Day10Question11.mp3: Department payroll analysis with LEFT JOIN! From departments left joined with employees, return department name, employee headcount, and total department payroll, handling empty departments.
questions.New_Day10Question11sol.mp3: Let's summarize department payroll. SELECT d.department_name, COUNT of e.employee_id AS headcount, COALESCE of SUM of e.salary, 0 AS total_payroll... FROM departments d LEFT JOIN employees e ON d.department_id = e.department_id... GROUP BY d.department_name... ORDER BY total_payroll DESC.
questions.New_Day10Question12.mp3: Filter joined records by calendar year! Join orders with customers for orders placed in the year 2024. Return order ID, customer first name, order date, and total amount.
questions.New_Day10Question12sol.mp3: Let's filter joined orders for 2024. SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name, o.order_date, o.total_amount... FROM orders o INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id... WHERE o.order_date >= '2024-01-01' AND o.order_date <= '2024-12-31'... ORDER BY o.order_date.
questions.New_Day10Question13.mp3: High-value customer orders! Join orders with customers where total amount is 50000 or greater. Return order ID, customer first name, customer region, and total amount.
questions.New_Day10Question13sol.mp3: Let's find high-value customer orders. SELECT o.order_id, c.first_name, c.region, o.total_amount... FROM orders o INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id... WHERE o.total_amount >= 50000... ORDER BY o.total_amount DESC.
questions.New_Day10Question14.mp3: Unsold products anti-join! Find products in our catalog that have never been ordered. Perform a LEFT JOIN from products to order items and filter where order item ID is null.
questions.New_Day10Question14sol.mp3: Let's find unsold products. SELECT p.product_id, p.name AS product_name, p.unit_price... FROM products p LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON p.product_id = oi.product_id... WHERE oi.id IS NULL.
questions.New_Day10Question15.mp3: Executive customer order rollups! Join customers with orders to return customer region, count of orders, and total revenue generated per region, sorted by revenue descending.
questions.New_Day10Question15sol.mp3: Let's summarize revenue by region. SELECT c.region, COUNT of o.order_id AS total_orders, SUM of o.total_amount AS regional_revenue... FROM customers c INNER JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id... GROUP BY c.region... ORDER BY regional_revenue DESC.
